user.title: Add an M-Bus
user.description: How is the M-Bus master connected to Home Assistant?

serial.title: M-Bus on a serial port
serial.description:
Path of the USB or RS232 M-Bus level converter wired to the bus.

Home Assistant must be able to open the port, and nothing else may hold it open — stop any other M-Bus tool first, the bus allows one master at a time.

data_description.baud: Almost every wired M-Bus meter runs at 2400 baud. The framing is always 8E1; even parity is not optional, and a meter will not answer at all without it.

tcp.title: M-Bus over a TCP bridge
tcp.description:
Address of a raw serial-to-TCP bridge in front of the M-Bus master — ser2net, socat, or a hardware serial-to-WiFi gateway.

The bridge must pass bytes through untouched and must be configured for 8E1 at the meters' baud rate; that setting lives on the bridge, not here. Only one master can use the bus at a time.

meters.title: Meters found
meters.description:
The scan found **{count}** meters. {scan_note}

Check the list before saving. You can edit it — one 16-digit secondary address per line — to add a meter the scan did not reach, or to remove one you do not want polled.

progress.scanning:
Searching the bus for meters — **{found} found so far**, now trying addresses starting `{prefix}`.

This is a wildcard address search and it is slow: expect several minutes for a few dozen meters at 2400 baud. There is no percentage because there is no honest one — how long a prefix takes depends on how many meters hide under it, which is what the search is working out.

It only runs when you add or reconfigure the bus, never on a restart.

error.cannot_connect: Nothing answered on the bus. Check the port or bridge address, that the framing is 8E1 at the right baud rate, that the M-Bus master has power, and that no other tool is holding the port.
error.bad_address: An M-Bus secondary address is exactly 16 hexadecimal digits, for example 0014280901060307. Put one per line.
error.no_meters: Enter at least one meter address.

data_description.scan_interval: One sweep costs roughly 0.7 seconds of bus time per meter at 2400 baud — about 30 seconds for 41 meters — and the bus is half-duplex, so reads cannot overlap. These are cumulative counters that move in hours, so there is little to gain from polling harder.
